entities.summary: Alan Basil de Lastic was a prominent Catholic clergyman in India who played a crucial role in the country's religious landscape. Born into a devout Christian family in the 1940s, de Lastic rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church to become the fourth Archbishop of Delhi in November 1990. He was instrumental in negotiating the 1992 Indo-Pakistani Treaty of Friendship, which helped to reduce tensions between the two nations. De Lastic's leadership and diplomatic efforts earned him international recognition, and he was awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian honor, in 1998. Despite his passing in 2000, de Lastic's legacy continues to be felt in India's Catholic community, with his successors working to build on his achievements. As de Lastic once said, 'The Church must be a beacon of hope in a world torn apart by conflict and division.'
